candidates.title: Theoretical Limits of Language Model Alignment
candidates.summary: Language model (LM) alignment improves model outputs to reflect human preferences while preserving the capabilities of the base model. The most common alignment approaches are (i) reinforcement learning, which maximizes the expected reward under a KL-divergence constraint, and (ii) best-of-NNN alignment, which selects the highest-reward output among NNN independent samples. Despite their widespread use, the fundamental limits of reward improvement under a KL budget remain poorly understood. candidates.title: vllm-project/vllm release: v0.34.0
candidates.summary: # v0.34.0 **1,061 commits from 412 contributors (120 new).** Thank you! ## TL;DR - **10 new models** (Mistral Large 4, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe, and more!) - **Extensible KV cache is on by default:** vLLM sizes the KV cache from memory actually free after warmup, so most models get a bigger cache and more throughput - in most cases you should now **remove `gpu_memory_utilization`** from your configs. - **Model Runner V1 is gone.** Model Runner V2 is now the only GPU runner. - **Big speedups** on Blackwell and MI355X: up to 1.95× decode (Step5 on GB200), 1.6× throughput

candidates.title: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems
candidates.summary: When a capable model and a human reviewer cooperate on the same decision, which human still adds value? We argue this is a question about a single cognitive trait, metacognitive calibration: the alignment between a reviewer's behavioral confidence and the actual correctness of their judgments. We develop a trait theory of reviewer value to make it precise. candidates.title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
candidates.summary: Real-world harness engineering is driven by explicit and implicit user requirements, which guide development and validation. However, existing harness evolution methods often overlook implicit requirements and interaction needs, while using a single evolution agent to modify the harness and benchmark scores to select changes. candidates.title: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game
candidates.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) now perform strongly on Alan Turing's 1950 Imitation Game, so we propose a harder challenge, the Personal Imitation Game, which asks whether a machine can replicate a specific individual in conversation rather than a generic human. Testing with 30 participants, we establish a human baseline and report the identity signals interrogators rely on: stylometric features, personality traits, and biographical facts. candidates.summary: Large language models have been widely used to generate plausible research ideas, yet it remains unclear what makes automated ideation effective and how generated novel proposals arise from prior scientific work. candidates.title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents
candidates.summary: User simulators offer a scalable way to evaluate interactive agents, but how to assess their quality remains underexplored. candidates.title: UltraTex: Aligning Physical Knowledge for High-Fidelity PBR Texture Generation
candidates.summary: Generating physically based rendering (PBR) texture maps for a 3D mesh from a single reference image is highly ambiguous, as the observed appearance entangles material identity, surface reflectance, and illumination. While current generative methods produce realistic albedo maps, they still struggle to infer accurate metallic and roughness attributes for relighting. We present UltraTex, a cascaded multi-view framework that moves beyond appearance matching by integrating physical knowledge into multi-view diffusion-based PBR generation. candidates.title: $Z$-sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling
candidates.summary: We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling. Video-based world action models (WAMs) show the value of joint future-and-action generation for control, yet inherit the heavy cost of video generators. Recent latent-space policies avoid pixel generation, yet typically align intermediate features or rely on frozen target encoders, decoupling future prediction from the VLM's native feature space. $Z$-sight instead predicts the future directly in the visual token space in which its VLM perceives the present.

candidates.title: Render the Robot, Generate the World: One Video World Model Across Embodiments
candidates.summary: Predicting the consequences of an agent's actions requires modeling both the body's motion and the environment's response. Most video world models attempt to learn both from numerical actions, even though geometry and kinematics already specify the intended motion.
